findings: legacyImportSender.ts (bulk CSV import path) sends only {orderId, amount} and omits the currency field entirely, even though it POSTs to the same /webhooks/order-created endpoint as the v2 payload.

consumer.ts calls payload.currency.toUpperCase() with no null/undefined guard, so any payload missing currency (every legacy-import webhook) throws unhandled -- this fully explains why crashes are limited to bulk-import orders and never normal checkout orders.

The v2 docs assert currency is 'always present,' but that's false in practice: legacyImportSender.ts predates v2 and was never updated to include it, so the documented contract and the actual code have silently diverged for one of the two producers.

Nothing enforces the documented v2 schema on the send side -- webhookSender.ts and legacyImportSender.ts both construct plain objects and POST them directly, with no shared schema/type or validation step that would catch legacyImportSender falling short of the v2 contract.

The payload carries no explicit version marker (e.g. a schemaVersion field), so a consumer has no way to detect at runtime whether it received the old (pre-currency) or new shape -- versioning exists only in documentation, not in the wire format.

Because legacyImportSender.ts sends amount with no currency, even a consumer that didn't crash would still have to guess the currency for bulk-import orders -- the missing field is a genuine data-ambiguity risk for financial processing, not just a crash trigger.

The bug is confined to one producer (legacy bulk import) that predates the v2 contract and was apparently never revisited when the schema changed, indicating no process existed to audit all producers when the payload contract was updated.
